# Run or resume an authorized goal

Use for eligible local work under an active goal. Reuse recorded evidence and keep each worker's brief bounded.

1. Read `tasktra goal --root <root> show <goal>`, `tasktra status --root <root>`, and the relevant work item. Stop if the goal is not active, the runtime is stopped, or authority is missing.
2. Create a scoped work unit with `tasktra work --root <root> create <goal> <title> --id <unit> --scope <scope.json> --checkpoint <current-checkpoint>` if none exists. Use the next pending checkpoint reported by goal/status output; omit `--checkpoint` only when the authority envelope has no checkpoints. A steward distinct from the performer records exact `work-claim` and `work-complete` approvals.
3. Generate a high-entropy token in the environment variable named by `--lease-token-env` (default `TASKTRA_LEASE_TOKEN`) without printing it. Claim with `tasktra work --root <root> claim <goal> --actor <performer> --envelope-sha256 <sha256> --repository <repo> --revision <rev> --branch <branch> --workspace <path>`. Claim stores only its hash and never emits the caller-supplied token; never put the token in prompts, files, logs, or command arguments.
4. To use a Codex child, first run `tasktra delegation --root <root> plan <routing-request.json> [--handoff <verified-handoff.json>]` and retain its bounded brief only in host memory. Preflight that the host exposes collaboration `spawn_agent`, `wait_agent`, and `list_agents`, that the resolved role pin is supported, and that the attempt is still live and not stopped. Then prepare exactly one receipt with `tasktra delegation --root <root> prepare <attempt> --actor <performer> --request <routing-request.json> --idempotency-key <key> --lease-token-env <env> [--handoff <verified-handoff.json>]`. Compare the retained plan and brief digests to prepare. Treat `launch_directive: invoke-once-now` as a one-use launch directive within the already approved attempt. An unfinished receipt holds runtime and goal capacity after its parent lease ends; a live parent and child count once, while a detached child holds one slot until its terminal receipt. `reconcile-only` means inspect the host tree by its deterministic `requested_task_name`; never call spawn again. A new key does not bypass an unresolved preparation.
5. For `invoke-once-now`, recheck that the lease is live and the runtime is not stopped, then call `collaboration.spawn_agent` once with the returned deterministic `task_name`, configured `agent_type`, `fork_turns: "none"`, and the bounded retained brief. Immediately record the exact returned canonical task name: `tasktra delegation --root <root> start <run> --actor <performer> --host-canonical-name <returned-task-name>`. Include `--host-agent-id` only when the host actually returned one. Do not manufacture an ID or call a peer-task creation API.
6. Observe the child final result with `collaboration.wait_agent` or the host's final delivery. Record its observed terminal outcome: for example, pipe the exact completed result bytes once to `tasktra delegation --root <root> finish <run> --actor <performer> --outcome completed --usage-status unavailable --result-stdin`. A missing result uses `result_status: unavailable`; completed requires an observed digest. Host/model usage remains unavailable unless the host supplies measured values. Inspect `tasktra delegation --root <root> show <run>` from a fresh Python process before finishing the parent work. Receipts are observations and never authenticate the host or approve work.
7. For an unresolved receipt, first inspect `tasktra delegation --root <root> unresolved [--goal-id <goal>]`. Use one actual `collaboration.list_agents` host-tree observation and only its exact canonical names. Normalize only a known `running` string or a completed object containing final text into the closed version-1 observation (`kind: tasktra.codex-host-tree-observation`). Reconcile once with `tasktra delegation --root <root> reconcile <run> --actor <performer> --observation <observation.json>`; for a completed object, pipe its exact final-text bytes to that command with `--result-stdin`. Then inspect `delegation show` from a fresh Python process. Do not respawn an unresolved launch, interrupt, cancel, abandon, or treat parent context as host or model authentication. Missing or unfamiliar host status stays unresolved and retains capacity. A completed receipt preserves parent status: an already blocked parent remains blocked, and a leased parent retains its slot until normal finish or recovery. Resolving the receipt only satisfies the execution-receipt prerequisite for a separately approved `work-requeue`. Historical non-null host IDs cannot be reconciled by the current host adapter.
For projects using the separate `execution` ledger, link native execution records to the parent work and exact host thread/turn IDs when those IDs are actually available. Refresh receipts only from the matching rollout; unavailable host identity or usage remains unavailable. These observations complement the lease-bound Codex receipts above and do not replace their capacity or completion gates.

8. Give a local worker only its objective, verified facts, evidence references, constraints, owned paths, budgets, and acceptance checks. Use `tasktra work ... heartbeat` before lease expiry when work is still valid. Validate through the Stage 2 workflow. Finish with `tasktra work --root <root> finish <attempt> --actor <performer> --outcome <class> --workflow <workflow.json> --evidence-json <evidence.json>` for success, or omit `--workflow` for a non-success outcome. Outcome classes are `transient`, `permanent`, `blocked`, `approval-required`, and `exhausted` as well as `success`.
9. Run `tasktra audit --root <root> verify`. On interruption use `tasktra work --root <root> recover --goal-id <goal>`; do not create a duplicate attempt or renew authority. Resume `blocked` or `approval-required` work only after a distinct approval for `work-requeue`, using `tasktra work --root <root> requeue <unit> --actor <performer> --envelope-sha256 <sha256> --evidence-json <evidence.json>`.

Pause at checkpoints, exhausted budgets, missing approvals, scope changes, or consequential effects. Return the work-unit and attempt IDs, measured usage, validation evidence, and next eligible action without exposing the lease token.
